explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Moses says the LORD your God “goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire…” Walls up to the heavens and giants on the other side, and Israel isn't sent in first. I'd follow that Leader anywhere.
Good guess, friend, but the text doesn't send any elders out front. Moses says the LORD your God goes across ahead of Israel. When the walls are that big, it matters who walks in first, and He does.
No spies in this part, friend. Moses doesn't mention a scouting party at all. He says the LORD your God goes across ahead of them as a consuming fire, and that's the whole plan.

Right on, baker. Moses says it twice: the LORD is driving these nations out “because of their wickedness.” He's making sure Israel doesn't walk in thinking they earned the land. That would be a hard head to bake around.

Hmm, the numbers actually point the other way. Moses says these are nations greater and stronger than Israel, with large cities fortified to the heavens. The reason he gives is their wickedness, not Israel's headcount.
Moses never says a word about their gods here, friend. He gives one reason: it's because of the wickedness of these nations. Israel's own righteousness isn't the reason either.

Yes, baker, promise. Moses says the LORD is driving them out to keep the promise He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The land comes down to a promise God made and keeps. Nobody on Israel's side of the counter has to take credit.

Close, but the word Moses uses is a different one. He says the LORD is keeping the promise He swore to their fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. A warning is something you give. A promise is something you keep, and He keeps it.

Law is a good Bible word, friend, but it isn't the one in this verse. Moses says the LORD is keeping the promise He swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The land comes from what He swore, and that's why it's a gift.

Not quite, baker. Moses says the opposite: “Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness.” He wants Israel to look back on purpose. Forgetting is exactly what he's telling them not to do.

That's right, baker. Moses says, “Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness.” He doesn't want them to forget it. A person who remembers where they've been is less likely to brag.

explanations.answer: Since the day they left Egypt
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Moses says, “From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.” That's a long stretch of rebelling. Friend, he isn't sugarcoating it.

Kadesh-barnea does come up later in this passage, but it isn't the starting line. Moses says Israel has been rebelling from the day they left the land of Egypt until they reached this place. So the story goes back a lot farther than that.

They haven't even crossed the Jordan yet, friend. That's what Moses is telling them today: they're about to. He says the rebelling has gone on from the day they left Egypt until they reached this place.
Yes, baker. Moses says, “I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.” That's a long time to be up there with the LORD. He gets the tablets of the covenant at the end of it.
Seven is a Bible favorite, friend, but not here. Moses says he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. That's way longer than a week.
Three days would be a short trip compared to this one. Moses says he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. He gets the tablets of the covenant at the end of it.

Right, baker. The tablets were “inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain…” Moses doesn't carve them himself. The writing is God's own.
The text gives no part in this to Joshua, friend. Moses says the tablets were “inscribed by the finger of God.” He names no helper for the writing.
Bezalel isn't in this passage, friend. Moses says the tablets were “inscribed by the finger of God.” Nobody else is credited with the lettering.

Not this time, baker. Moses says the tablets were inscribed with “the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.” The people had already heard those words. Now they're written down.

That's right, baker. The tablets carry “the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.” The people had heard them already. Now those same words are written in stone.

Yes, baker, image. The LORD says, “They have made for themselves a molten image.” He also says how quickly they've turned aside from the way He commanded them. Moses was only up the mountain forty days.
An altar is a good guess, friend, but that's not the word. The LORD says they have made for themselves a molten image. It's a made thing that stands in the place of God.
No throne in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “They have made for themselves a molten image.” A little later Moses calls it a molten calf.

True, baker. The LORD says, “Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.” That's what He says right after telling Moses to leave Him alone so He may destroy them. Moses doesn't take it. Hang on to that for the next stop.

It's in the text, friend. The LORD says to Moses, “Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.” He says it right after telling Moses to leave Him alone so He may destroy the people. It's a big offer sitting right there.

explanations.answer: Throws them down and shatters them
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Moses says, “So I took the two tablets and threw them out of my hands, shattering them before your eyes.” The people watched it happen. He'd just carried those tablets all the way down the mountain.

explanations.answer: Hides them away in his tent
explanations.explanation: No tent in this scene, friend. Moses says he threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them before the people's eyes. He wasn't hiding anything.

explanations.answer: Holds them high over the people
explanations.explanation: Nothing gets held up here, friend. Moses says he took the two tablets and threw them out of his hands, shattering them before the people's eyes. He did it right where they could see.

Right, baker. Moses says, “I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you.” He wasn't scared for himself. I think that tells you where his heart was.
Moses doesn't say that, friend. He says he was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against the people, enough to destroy them. His fear was about what the LORD might do.
The mountain was blazing with fire earlier, but that's not what Moses names here. He says he was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against the people. That's the fear he gives.
Moses says the opposite, baker. Right after the fear, he adds, “But the LORD listened to me this time as well.” The LORD heard him the first time too. He listens to Moses both times.

That's right, baker. Moses says, “But the LORD listened to me this time as well.” That little “as well” tells you the LORD listened the first time too. Moses was on his face and the LORD still heard him.

True, baker. Moses says, “The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.” Aaron was in real trouble, and his brother prayed for him anyway. That's a good brother.
It's right there in the text, friend. Moses says the LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, “but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.” Moses covered his brother in prayer.

explanations.answer: Burns it and grinds it to dust
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Moses says, “I took that sinful thing, the calf you had made, and burned it in the fire. Then I crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust…” Nothing of that calf was left to keep. He finished the job.

explanations.answer: Buries it at the mountain's foot
explanations.explanation: No burying in this telling, friend. Moses says he burned the calf in the fire, crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust. Then he cast it into the stream that came down from the mountain.

explanations.answer: Breaks it and hides the pieces
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't hide anything, friend. He says he burned the calf in the fire, crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust. Then he threw it into the stream that came down from the mountain.
That's the word, baker. Moses says, “You neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.” The LORD had said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.” They didn't trust Him and they didn't go.
Close in feeling, friend, but not the word Moses uses. He says, “You neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.” The LORD told them to go up and possess the land, and they rebelled against the command.
They heard Him fine, friend. The LORD said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.” What Moses says is that they neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.

Yes, baker. Moses prays, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.” He asks for the people before he asks for anything else. Notice he calls them the LORD's own people.
That was the LORD's offer, friend, not Moses' request. The LORD had said He'd make Moses into a nation mightier and greater than the people. Moses opens his prayer with “do not destroy Your people.”

explanations.answer: Send the people back to Egypt
explanations.explanation: Moses doesn't ask for that, friend. He prays, “do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance,” and reminds the LORD that He brought them out of Egypt with a mighty hand. Going back isn't in the prayer.
Right, baker. Moses prays, “Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” He points back to the promise made to them, not to anything the people have earned. That's a smart place to stand.
Nice word, friend, but not the one in the prayer. Moses says, “Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” He's asking the LORD to bring those three to mind.
Reward isn't in this prayer, friend. Moses says, “Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Then he asks the LORD to overlook the stubbornness of the people.

explanations.answer: He couldn't bring them into the land
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Moses says they'll say, “Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land He had promised them…” He also says they'll claim the LORD hated Israel and brought them out to kill them in the wilderness. Moses is thinking about how it would look to the people they left behind.

explanations.answer: He was never with them at all
explanations.explanation: That isn't what Moses says they'd say, friend. He says they'd claim the LORD was not able to bring Israel into the land He had promised. They'd also say He hated them and brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.

explanations.answer: He wanted them to stay in Egypt
explanations.explanation: Not quite, friend. Moses says they would claim the LORD was not able to bring Israel into the promised land, and that He hated them. They would say He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark of wood.” That ark is where the tablets will go. Moses has a carpentry job and a chiseling job.
Stone is for the tablets, friend. The LORD tells Moses to chisel out two stone tablets and make an ark of wood. No altar is named in these verses.
No lampstand in this verse, friend. The LORD tells Moses to chisel out two stone tablets and make an ark of wood. That's the one extra thing.

True, baker. The LORD says, “I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke; and you are to place them in the ark.” The words come back the same. The broken tablets don't cancel what He said.

The text says it plainly, friend. The LORD says, “I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.” He tells Moses to place them in the ark. Same words, new stones.

That's right, baker. The LORD wrote “the Ten Commandments that He had spoken to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly.” He wrote what He'd said before. Those words are the same ones the people had heard.
Prophecies don't show up here, friend. The text says the LORD wrote the Ten Commandments that He had spoken to the people out of the fire. That's what was written the first time.

No visions on these tablets, friend. The LORD wrote the Ten Commandments that He had spoken on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly. They're the same ones that had been written before.
Moses says something different, baker. He went back down the mountain and “placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me.” They didn't go in a tent. They went in the ark.

That's right, baker. Moses says, “I went back down the mountain and placed the tablets in the ark I had made, as the LORD had commanded me; and there they have remained.” They went in the ark, not a tent.

Yes, baker, blessings. The LORD set apart Levi “to carry the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name, as they do to this day.” Speaking blessings is part of the job. That's not a bad thing to have on a work description.
Oaths aren't in the job description, friend. The text says Levi is set apart to carry the ark, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name. Blessings are the word.

Moses did his own fasting earlier, friend, but fasts aren't in this verse. Levi is set apart to carry the ark, to stand before the LORD to serve Him, and to pronounce blessings in His name. That's the third piece.

That's it, baker. Moses says, “That is why Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers; the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God promised him.” Levi doesn't get a share of land. He gets the LORD Himself.

explanations.answer: Levi gave his share to Aaron
explanations.explanation: The text gives a different reason, friend. Moses says Levi has no portion or inheritance among his brothers because the LORD is his inheritance. He says the LORD promised it to him.

explanations.answer: Levi already had land in Egypt
explanations.explanation: Egypt doesn't come into it, friend. Moses says, “the LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God promised him.” That's why Levi has no portion among his brothers.

explanations.answer: Lead the people on toward the land
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people, that they may enter and possess the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.” The mountain time is over. It's time to move.

explanations.answer: Stay up on the mountain longer
explanations.explanation: The LORD says the opposite, friend. He tells Moses, “Get up. Continue your journey ahead of the people.” Moses has already spent plenty of time up there.

explanations.answer: Take the people back to Horeb
explanations.explanation: Horeb is behind them, friend. The LORD tells Moses to continue his journey ahead of the people so they may enter and possess the land He swore to their fathers. They're heading toward the land.
